body.p: The Oxygen AI Positron Hooks add-on provides a ready-to-use implementation of the AI hooks extension point. It reads a JSON configuration file and invokes external scripts (Python, shell, PowerShell, etc.) whenever AI Positron hook events fire. This lets you connect AI lifecycle events to your own tooling (for auditing, policy enforcement, or analytics) without writing Java code.The Oxygen AI Positron Hooks add-on is compatible with Oxygen XML Editor/Author/Developer version 28.1 or newer and with all versions of the Oxygen AI Positron add-on 9.0 and newer.

section.title: Installation
section.p:
To install this add-on, follow this procedure:
Go to Help Install new add-ons to open an add-on selection dialog box. Enter or paste https://www.oxygenxml.com/InstData/Addons/default/updateSite.xml in the Show add-ons from field or select it from the drop-down menu.
Select the Oxygen AI Positron Hooks add-on and click Next.
Read the end-user license agreement. Then select the I accept all terms of the end-user license agreement option and click Install.
Restart the application.
Result: The Options Preferences AI Positron Hooks preferences page becomes available and the add-on starts dispatching hook events to the scripts configured in the JSON file.

The add-on can also be installed using the following alternative installation procedure:
Go to the Releases page and download the oxygen-ai-positron-hooks-addon-{version}-plugin.jar file.
Unzip it inside {oXygenInstallDir}/plugins. Make sure you do not create any intermediate folders. After unzipping the archive, the file system should look like this: {oXygenInstallDir}/plugins/oxygen-ai-positron-hooks-addon-x.y.z, and inside this folder there should be a plugin.xml file.

section.title: Configuration File
section.p: After installation, configure the add-on by pointing it to a JSON configuration file. Open Options Preferences AI Positron Hooks and set the path to the configuration file. The default value is ${pd}/ai-positron-hooks.json (project directory). Editor variables such as ${pd}, ${oxygenInstallDir}, and ${homeDir} are expanded before the path is resolved. If the file does not exist, the add-on starts without any active hooks and no error is shown. A parse error in an existing file is reported on the preferences page.
The configuration file maps hook event names to lists of script commands:

Each hook entry has the following fields:
command The shell command to execute. Quoted tokens are supported (for example, "python3 \"my path/run.py\"").
timeout Maximum execution time in seconds. Defaults to 30. The process is forcibly terminated when this limit is exceeded.
Multiple commands per event are supported. They run sequentially. Execution stops on the first failure.

section.title: Supported Hook Events
section.p: Use the event's name as the key in the configuration file. For the full list of available events, their payload structure, and whether they are blocking, see Hook Events Reference.

section.title: Script Invocation Contract
section.p: When a hook fires, the add-on runs each configured command.

ul.li: The event payload JSON is written to the script's stdin. Refer to Intercepting AI Events Using Hooks for the full payload field reference.
The working directory is the directory that contains the configuration file.
For blocking hooks, a non-zero exit code throws an exception that vetoes the action. The script's combined stdout/stderr becomes the exception message displayed to the user.
For fire-and-forget hooks, a non-zero exit code is logged but does not interrupt AI Positron.
The timeout value forcibly terminates the script if it runs longer than allowed.

section.title: Preferences Page
section.p:
Open Options Preferences AI Positron Hooks to:
Set the configuration file path (type directly or use the browse button to pick a file).
View configuration load errors.
Browse the active hook-to-command mappings loaded from the current file.
Monitor a live execution log (newest first, maximum 500 entries) and clear it with the Clear button.

section.title: Source Code
section.p: The source code of this add-on is publicly available on GitHub: . You can use it as a reference or starting point for building your own hook handler add-on in Java.
